- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict spikes; increase forecast for next 3–5 days by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending up, model often overcorrects downward; adjust downward bias by 15–30% for next 3–7 days.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome, model frequently overestimates the peak and underestimates the subsequent decline — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 20–40% for next 2–4 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67) and history shows mean reversion, model often fails to revert — apply a “mean-reversion” heuristic: forecast should align with 30-day moving average of history for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is rising — apply a “sentiment multiplier”: multiply forecast by 1.15–1.30 if sentiment > 0.67 in last 5 days.
- If model shows “early peak” (forecast peaks before true peak), it’s often due to sentiment overestimating momentum — delay peak forecast by 1–3 days if sentiment is rising.
- When sentiment is negative and model forecasts are low, avoid “over-shrinking” — add 5–10% to forecast if sentiment is trending upward from 0.33–0.67.
